step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates Level Beyond's Media to Cloud ingest pipeline and metadata extraction architecture. A User uploads raw video files directly into an Amazon S3 bucket. This file creation event triggers AWS Step Functions, which acts as the orchestrator. In the first phase of the workflow, AWS Step Functions kicks off Amazon Elemental MediaConvert to generate browser-compatible video proxies. In parallel, Step Functions invokes AWS Lambda to compute checksums and capture basic media metadata. Both MediaConvert and Lambda store this initial technical metadata in Amazon DynamoDB. Concurrently, Step Functions triggers Amazon Rekognition to extract celebrity tracking, violence, and visual metadata indexed to video timecodes, storing it in DynamoDB. Step Functions also triggers Amazon Transcribe to translate audio into text. This text is processed by Amazon Comprehend to extract entities and detect profanity, which is saved in DynamoDB. Lastly, DynamoDB functions as a temporary datastore from which metadata is ingested into the Reach Engine platform running on Amazon EC2 and Amazon EKS environments for indexing, search, and video monetization workflows.

nodes.name: User
nodes.notes: Uploads source video content from camera cards or remote devices.

nodes.name: AWS Step Functions
nodes.notes: Orchestrates video proxy creation, visual ML analysis, and audio translation workflows.

nodes.name: AWS Elemental MediaConvert
nodes.notes: Generates low-resolution browser-friendly video proxies for preview and visual verification.

nodes.name: AWS Lambda
nodes.notes: Serverless function triggered by Step Functions to calculate video checksums and extract technical metadata.

nodes.name: Amazon Rekognition
nodes.notes: Extracts timecoded visual metadata including celebrities, nudity, and safety tags.

nodes.name: Amazon Transcribe
nodes.notes: Converts the audio track from the media file into raw text transcripts.

nodes.name: Amazon Comprehend
nodes.notes: Performs Natural Language Processing to extract key entities and pinpoint occurrences of profanity.

nodes.name: Amazon DynamoDB
nodes.notes: A temporary NoSQL store holding aggregated visual, technical, and linguistic metadata until ingested into Reach Engine.

nodes.name: Amazon EC2
nodes.notes: Part of the Reach Engine hosting platform, providing scalable virtual servers for media orchestration.

nodes.name: Amazon EKS
nodes.notes: Part of the Reach Engine hosting platform, orchestrating container workloads for video search, playback, and monetization UI.
